questions.q: What does a job role represent?
options: A general classification true of a person regardless of their job
A specific job function tied to a real job title, such as Accounts Payable Manager
A single privilege, such as voiding a payment
A data security policy with no function security attached
questions.explain: A job role maps to a specific job function or title and is built by combining duty roles that cover that job's needs.

questions.q: Which of the following is a classic example of an abstract role?
options: Accounts Payable Manager
General Ledger Accountant
Employee
US Business Unit Payables Data Role
questions.explain: Employee is the most common abstract role — it's granted regardless of specific job title and covers access every worker needs.

questions.q: What does a data role add on top of a job role?
options: Nothing; a data role and a job role are identical
An additional password requirement
A new privilege unrelated to the job role's function security
A specific data scope, such as limiting payables access to one business unit
questions.explain: A data role inherits the job role's function security and layers a data scope on top, such as restricting access to a particular business unit.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes a job role from an abstract role?
options: A job role describes a specific job function; an abstract role describes a general classification independent of job
A job role describes what kind of person someone is; an abstract role describes their specific job
They are two names for the exact same thing
Only abstract roles can be provisioned to users
questions.explain: Job roles map to specific job functions. Abstract roles describe a general classification (like Employee) that applies regardless of specific job.

questions.q: Why are data roles more central to HCM security than to Financials security in most implementations?
options: Financials does not support any form of data scoping
Data roles are only usable with abstract roles, which HCM has more of
HCM commonly auto-generates data roles per department or business unit, while Financials more often scopes data through data access sets and business unit assignment
Oracle disabled data roles for all Financials modules
questions.explain: Financials typically controls data scope through data access sets and direct business unit assignment, covered in Chapter 2, rather than through generated data roles as HCM commonly does.
